sections.abstract: Block Discrete Denoising Diffusion Language Models (BD3-LMs) interpolate between discrete denoising diffusion and autoregressive (AR) models to overcome limitations in likelihood modeling and fixed-length generation. BD3-LMs support flexible-length sequences and improve inference efficiency via KV caching and parallel token sampling. The authors introduce an efficient training algorithm, gradient variance estimators, and data-driven noise schedules to minimize training variance. BD3-LMs achieve state-of-the-art performance among diffusion models on language modeling benchmarks and enable the generation of arbitrary-length sequences.
sections.introduction: Diffusion models offer parallelized generation and controllability but face three challenges in discrete data: fixed-length constraints, inability to use KV caching, and a perplexity gap compared to AR models. BD3-LMs address these by defining an autoregressive distribution over blocks of tokens, where each block is modeled by a discrete denoising diffusion process. This framework builds on D3PM and MDLM, extending them to arbitrary lengths and addressing the perplexity gap through gradient variance analysis. Unlike Gaussian diffusion over embeddings, this discrete approach allows for tractable likelihood estimates and maintains bidirectional context within blocks while preserving autoregressive structure between blocks.
sections.method:
The paper defines discrete variables in space $\mathcal{V} = \{\mathbf{x} \in \{0, 1\}^V : \sum_i x_i = 1\} \subset \Delta^V$. BD3-LMs group tokens into $B$ blocks $\mathbf{x}^b$ of length $L'$, factorizing the likelihood as $\log p_	heta(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{b=1}^B \log p_	heta(\mathbf{x}^b | \mathbf{x}^{<b})$. Each block uses a reverse process $p_	heta(\mathbf{x}^b_s | \mathbf{x}^b_t, \mathbf{x}^{<b}) = \sum_{\mathbf{x}^b} q(\mathbf{x}^b_s | \mathbf{x}^b_t, \mathbf{x}^b) p_	heta(\mathbf{x}^b | \mathbf{x}^b_t, \mathbf{x}^{<b})$. The training objective is $\mathcal{L}_{BD}(\mathbf{x}; 	heta) := \sum_{b=1}^B \mathbb{E}_{t \sim [0,1]} \mathbb{E}_q [  rac{\alpha'_t}{1-\alpha_t} \log p_	heta(\mathbf{x}^b | \mathbf{x}^b_t, \mathbf{x}^{<b}) ]$. To address the perplexity gap, the authors analyze gradient variance $	ext{Var}_{\mathbf{X},t} [
abla_	heta l(\mathbf{X}; 	heta)] \approx  rac{1}{M-1} \sum_{m=1}^M \| 
abla_	heta l(\mathbf{X}^m; 	heta) -  rac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M 
abla_	heta l(\mathbf{X}^m; 	heta) \|_2^2$. They propose 'clipped' noise schedules $\mathcal{U}[ eta, \omega]$ optimized via $\min_{ eta,\omega} 	ext{Var}_{\mathbf{X},t} [\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{X}; 	heta,  eta, \omega)]$ to reduce variance. A vectorized training algorithm uses specialized attention masks to compute the loss in a single pass.
sections.experiments: BD3-LMs are evaluated on LM1B and OpenWebText (OWT). The architecture consists of a 110M parameter transformer with 12 layers, trained using AdamW with a $3e-4$ learning rate. Likelihood evaluation utilizes low-discrepancy samplers. Zero-shot generalization is tested on PTB, Wikitext, and Pubmed. The implementation uses PyTorch's FlexAttention for optimized sparse masking and kernel fusion, and the vectorized training algorithm is compared against naive implementations for speed-up analysis.
sections.results: BD3-LMs set a new SOTA for diffusion models, outperforming SEDD and MDLM by up to 13% in perplexity. On OWT, BD3-LMs with $L'=4$ achieve a perplexity of $\le 20.73$. The models demonstrate superior zero-shot performance on Pubmed, even surpassing AR models. Qualitatively, BD3-LMs generate coherent sequences up to 10k tokens, far exceeding training context. Ablations confirm that clipped noise schedules effectively minimize training variance, correlating with improved test perplexity. The vectorized training algorithm provides a 20-25% speed-up, while FlexAttention yields a $\approx 5\times$ speedup in attention computation.
sections.conclusion: BD3-LMs successfully bridge the gap between diffusion and autoregressive models by combining block-wise diffusion with an AR framework. The approach enables arbitrary-length generation and efficient inference via KV caching. By identifying and mitigating gradient variance through optimized noise schedules, the authors achieve state-of-the-art discrete diffusion performance. Future work may further explore the scaling properties of block-causal diffusion architectures.
sections.supplementary: The supplementary provides the full Negative ELBO derivation: $-\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) \le \sum_{b=1}^B [\mathcal{L}_{recons} + \mathcal{L}_{diffusion} + \mathcal{L}_{prior}]$. It includes proofs that for $L'=1$, the model recovers the AR NLL and that the NELBO is tight ($\mathcal{L}_K \le \mathcal{L}_{K+1}$). The full attention mask is defined as $M_{\text{full}} = \begin{bmatrix} M_{BD} & M_{OBC} \\ 0 & M_{BC} \end{bmatrix}$, where $M_{BD}$ is block-diagonal, $M_{OBC}$ is offset block-causal, and $M_{BC}$ is block-causal. Qualitative samples compare MDLM, BD3-LM, and AR models across various lengths.
